picks.title: Australia May Legalize AI Training on Your Books. Sign a Statement Opposing It.
picks.excerpt: The Australian government has announced that it is planning to introduce legislation that would change copyright law to allow AI companies to use authors' work, without a license, to build their models. This would apply to authors from anywhere in […]
picks.rationale: New government action: Australia plans a copyright bill that would let AI companies train on authors' books without a licence, and it would apply to authors anywhere. The Authors Guild is collecting signatures against it.

picks.title: Chakrabarty Paper Dropped from OpenAI Suit
picks.excerpt: Chakrabarty market dilution paper dropped from OpenAI copyright case. CEATL survey finds 30% of literary translators lost assignments to AI.
picks.rationale: The market-dilution study that OpenAI tried to exclude is now out of the authors' copyright case, which weakens a key damages argument. A new CEATL survey also finds 30% of literary translators have lost work to AI.

picks.title: Making a Writing Prompt for Gemini Argon - Novelcrafter Live
picks.excerpt: Novelcrafter's live session spends time with Google's new Gemini Argon model, working out by trial and error how to prompt it for fiction writing inside the Novelcrafter writing app.
picks.rationale: Hands-on and usable right away: the Novelcrafter team shows how to write fiction prompts for Google's new Gemini Argon model inside a writing app many authors already use.

picks.title: Guest Post - All this AI Signal and Noise: What Deserves Action Now
picks.excerpt: Amidst the onslaught of industry and global changes, opportunities, and advancements, which signals deserve action now, which are context, and which are weather?
picks.rationale: A triage framework for publishers: it sorts current AI developments into ones to act on now, ones that are background context, and ones that are noise. Freely readable.
